title: dedicated gpu pool autoscale warmup investigation breadcrumbs
content:
Quick breadcrumbs / scratchpad from investigating the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale + warmup thrash we've been seeing (Feb 24 - Mar 4). Mostly notes to self and steps other folks can follow.

Summary of the symptom:
- Clients hit increased tail latency around 08:30 PST on 2026-02-24 and again intermittently.
- Autoscaler repeatedly spun up new nodes, then scale-downs happened soon after; overall capacity oscillated (thrash).
- New nodes often reported long model load times (90-240s) causing requests to queue and triggering additional scale-ups.
- Observed several "cold start" errors in proxy logs: "streaming timeout waiting for runtime ready" and repeated 503s.

Hypothesis (current):
1) Autoscaler aggressively scales based on short-window CPU/queue metrics (policy = bursty-window-30s). Short spikes cause scale-ups.
2) Model warmup is not deterministic and occasionally hits slow pulls (container image pull + model download + quantized weight conversion).
3) New nodes become Ready but runtime isn't fully warmed (runtime readiness probe passing before KV cache/model fully loaded).
4) Rapid scale-downs (policy: idle-terminate-120s) kills partially warmed nodes; when traffic spikes again, we lose invested warm caches -> thrash.
5) There might be a scheduling mismatch where new pods land on nodes with insufficient NVidia driver/kmod state causing longer init (seen "nvidia-smi: command not found" in some init logs before driver modules modprobe succeeded).

Commands I ran (most useful ones first):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime\  # look for recent restarts/long init
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood-serving  # check events (ImagePullBackOff, FailedMount, etc.)
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> -c runtime --since=2h
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> -c sidecar --previous
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-gpu -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node>  # look for kubelet errors, taints, conditions
- gcloud compute ssh <node> --zone=us-west1-b --command "sudo journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -n 200"
- gcloud compute ssh <node> --zone=us-west1-b --command "nvidia-smi || echo 'no nvidia'"
- docker pull <model-image> && time docker run --rm <model-image> /bin/bash -c 'ls /models && cat /models/model.sha'  # measure image startup/model unpack time locally

Key logs / error snippets I saved here:
- proxy logs: "2026-02-24T08:29:12Z ERROR request-id=abcd streaming timeout waiting for runtime ready after 180s"
- runtime init: "2026-02-24T08:29:14Z INFO loading model weights (quantized) - estimated size 32GB" then "2026-02-24T08:31:45Z WARN memory pressure, attempting gc"
- kubelet: "Failed to start container runtime: context deadline exceeded" on node boot (timed at ~30s)
- image pull: "Back-off pulling image" seen on ~10% of boots (network flakiness suspected)

Observed metrics during incident (approx):
- average model load time for new pod: 120s (p90=230s, p50=95s)
- disk I/O bursts correlated with load spikes
- cache hit rate for prefix cache: dropped from 80% -> 12% after scale-down

Repro steps (local-ish):
1) Start single-node dedicated pool with autoscale policy = bursty-window-30s, target-util=0.6, min=1, max=8.
2) Fire synthetic burst: 500 concurrent small requests for a short window (10-30s).
3) Observe scale up events (new node creation), watch pods scheduled and model load timings.
4) After burst, quickly drop traffic to 0 and wait 90-150s. Observe scale-down.
5) Repeat bursts: should reproduce thrash in ~3-4 cycles if image/model download slower than 60s.

Things tried (and results):
- Increased idle-terminate from 120s -> 300s for a subset of pools (A/B test). Result: thrash reduced but cost increased ~+18% for that pool. Tail latency improved during repeated bursts.
- Add readiness probe to runtime that checks model cache hotness (endpoint /internal/ready returns 200 only when model loaded). Result: fewer 503s, but some pods still passed readiness too early because the probe relied on the runtime process only, not model weights fully loaded.
- Pre-pulling images via DaemonSet on new nodes: added a lightweight init daemon that runs on boot to pull model images. Result: reduced ImagePullBackOffs but didn't eliminate long model load times (weights unpack + quantization steps still expensive).
- Warm start: used a Kubernetes Job to pre-warm model by starting a runtime process and doing a small inference loop (warm HTTP calls). This reduced per-pod cold start time by ~30-40% when successful. However, it added extra complexity and sometimes failed because Job scheduling competed with normal pods during scale-up.
- Increase node provisioning CPU/memory for init step (larger machine type for init-only): improved unpack time but not enough in worst-case network scenarios.

Notable weirdness / anomalies:
- Several nodes reported kernel OOPS in dmesg around NVidia driver init. Those nodes took ~5-10m to become fully usable. Need to correlate with specific instance images (ami-id) and driver version.
- One region's image registry had slower egress on 2026-02-25 02:00-03:30 UTC (reported by infra monitoring). Correlates with spike.
- Autoscaler metrics were observing high queue length derived from request queue (sidecar), but sidecar CPU was pegged leading to mis-reported readiness. Might need a decoupled metric (queue length + runtime acceptance rate).

Short-term mitigations (to apply quickly):
- Increase min nodes for high-traffic pools from 1 -> 2 to avoid complete loss of warm caches for small bursty customers.
- Adjust autoscaler cooldown/aggregation window: use 2-3m aggregation for scale decisions rather than 30s bursty window for pools serving bursty-but-repeating traffic.
- Add a model-warm readiness gate: k8s readiness only true after /internal/ready AND model-sha matches expected. Requires runtime expose.
- Pre-warm step using a horizontal Job with nodeSelector:pool=dedicated-gpu, run only when new node detected (watch node add event). Simpler alternative: maintain one warm preloader pod per node via DaemonSet with a lower priorityClass so it doesn't steal capacity from real pods.

Longer-term ideas (design level):
- Introduce "warmth" scoring in scheduler/pool: nodes have warm caches metadata; scheduler prefers nodes with higher warmth for routing new requests. Integrate with smart routing (fall back to warmed models).
- Keep a small always-on pool of warmed mini-inference containers that can proxy requests to full runtimes while they finish loading (fast path returns cheap fallback until model warmed).
- Improve model artifact packaging to avoid expensive runtime conversions on first start (ship converted quantized weights, checksumed).
- Cache model layers across tenants (shared read-only volume) to reduce per-node unpack. Needs isolation/rules for cross-tenant models.

Next steps / TODOs (who -> what -> by when):
- (Diego) correlate node boot logs with AMI/driver versions and open infra ticket if a specific AMI is flaky. Due 2026-03-06.
- (Priya) implement a conservative autoscale policy for the test pool and run A/B for 72h. Due 2026-03-05.
- (Samir) prototype k8s readiness gate that checks model-sha and model-cache-hotness. Provide PR for runtime by 2026-03-10.
- (Ava) collect per-boot image pull durations across regions and add to the incident timeline. Due 2026-03-07.

Useful snippets (pasteable):
# check recent pods that restarted a lot
kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | grep dedicated-gpu

# example readiness probe (temp)
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /internal/ready?require_model=true
    port: 8081
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 10

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a messy breadcrumbs file; main output is the hypotheses + quick mitigations that we can flip fast.
- If we decide to change autoscale policy cluster-wide, coordinate with cost analysis (finance) and alerting (SRE).
- We should add synthetic traffic tests to CI that simulate bursty traffic and assert 95th latency under autoscale policy changes.

Links / refs:
- Infra PR for image prefetching: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/689
- JIRA: JIRA-RI-1423 (incident timeline + postmortem stub)
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime thread starting 2026-02-24

End of breadcrumbs.

(If you copy anything for the postmortem, please sanitize internal hostnames/ids.)
